topic: Forces and Their Effects on Motion
key_concepts: Force is operationally defined by its observed effects on motion
Forces do not always cause motion
Force can start, speed up, slow down, stop, or change the direction of an object
Force is described by magnitude, direction, point of application, and line of action
Contact forces include applied force, friction, normal force, and tension
Non-contact forces include gravitational and magnetic forces
Friction always opposes motion; air resistance is a frictional force
Gravitational force depends on mass and distance; weight is an example of gravitational fo
Magnetic poles exert attraction or repulsion; opposite poles attract and like poles repel
Balanced forces are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction and do not change motion
Unbalanced forces cause a change in an object's motion
